To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lectins can be used to study the glycoconjugate content of normal lymphoid tissues, and that this information can be used to elucidate the nature of the extracellular matrix of germinal centres and the unusual glycoconjugated structures of the Reed-Sternberg cell.

the lectin binding patterns in germinal centres are compatible with the idea of active secretion of a pericellular domain, and the lectin binding pattern in the Reed-Sternberg cell suggests that the nucleolus contains glycoconjugate of diverse structure.

lectin histochemistry is a useful technique for studying the structure and function of lymphoid tissues, that the extracellular matrix of germinal centres has a unique composition and that this is related to their function, and that the Reed-Sternberg cell is an unusual cell with a distinctive carbohydrate rich cytoplasm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of lectins as tools in histopathological diagnosis and the elucidation of their role in lymphoid tissues.

the application of lectins as histochemical tools to investigate normal and neoplasia lymphoid tissue, in order to obtain information about the structure and function of the carbohydrate rich extracellular domains and cell surfaces.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lectin histochemistry is a valuable adjunct to conventional histology, and may provide a useful means of identifying and characterizing the cell populations in lymphoid tissues.
lectin binding studies are useful in the investigation of normal and neoplasia lymphoid tissues.

lectins are not a panacea for lymphocyte classification, although they can be of value in some circumstances, and they are of particular value in the study of the extracellular matrix of germinal centres and the Reed-Sternberg cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lectins have a role in histopathological diagnosis and that they may provide new insights into the pathogenesis of Hodgkin's disease and other lymphomas.
lectin histochemistry can be used to detect subtle changes in carbohydrate structure which may reflect important changes in cell behaviour.
in normal lymph nodes lectins are useful in the identification of germinal centres, the marginal zones and the mantle zones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lectins can be used to study the glycoconjugate composition of cells in situ, and that the patterns obtained can be used to draw inferences about the structure and function of the cells involved.

the use of lectins as histochemical probes in the study of lymphoid tissues can be very informative and that they can be combined with other histochemical methods to give a more complete picture of cellular structure.
the lectin binding patterns in lymphoid tissues are complex, and that they are likely to reflect a wide diversity of carbohydrate structures.
